mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% over the next month leads to a one-month forward S&P 500 return of approximately +0.5% due to market anticipation of future rate hikes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite CPIAUCSL crossing 0.3%, or the effect is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% for two consecutive months increases the expected future wage growth for S&P 500 firms, which boosts equity valuations and drives positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Payrolls growth reverts to ≤0.5% for ≥3 months without a subsequent positive 20-day SPX return, or IC < 0.05 over 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in monthly INDPRO manufacturing index below 50 (indicating supply-side weakness) precedes a 5-day forward S&P 500 decline as investors anticipate reduced corporate profit margins.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 50 in the following trading day
failure_condition: INDPRO reverts to ≥50 within 3 days without a negative 5-day SPX return, or IC > 0.2 over a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST retail sales above 2% in the following month predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return of +1% as it signals resilient consumer demand and optimistic earnings expectations.
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive 20-day return after HOUST crosses 2%, or IC < 0.1 over 6 months after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, the S&P 500 exhibits a negative 60-day forward return as markets price in higher future borrowing costs and tighter liquidity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or IC > 0.05 over 12 months after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4% for three consecutive months increases the probability of wage growth underestimation by central banks, prompting a 20-day S&P 500 positive return as investors anticipate rate cuts.
regime_hint: labor market slack or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain negative despite UNRATE staying below 4%, or IC < 0.1 over 6 months in such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both RSAFS and INDPRO by at least 5% in the same month indicate supply-side stress, which predicts a 5-day S&P 500 negative return as profit margin expectations fall.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < INDPRO baseline and INDPRO < 95% of INDPRO previous month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negative despite both proxies falling, or IC > 0.2 over 3 months after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 3.5% for 4 consecutive months), a 60-day S&P 500 forward return of +2% is expected as markets anticipate future equity-friendly policy and lower risk aversion.
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain flat or negative despite easing, or IC < 0.05 over 12 months in such regimes.
